_provider_api_note: Story 28.1: Piano Analytics Data Query API v3 is pinned HERE and only here. connector.py builds every URL from provider_api_base + provider_api_version (POST /v3/data/getData). api_catalog.json / catalog_sources.json api_version must equal this pin.

_error_map_note: Reference: Piano Analytics 'Error codes' (developers.piano.io/analytics/data-api/technical-information/error-codes/), the published API-Code / HTTP-status table, re-read 2026-08-17. KEYS ARE '<http_status>:<API_Code_Category>' -- the CATEGORY PREFIX only. A Piano v3 body carries an API-Code string shaped Category_Subcode; connector._extract_api_code() reads it and connector._code_prefix() reduces it to the Category, then feeds classify_http_error a payload whose top-level 'code' IS that Category, so a full Category_Subcode key would be unreachable and is never written here. WHAT THE KEYS BUY -- five of them change a verdict core cannot reach on the status alone, and every one is read straight off the published table: '400:DataNotReady' ('The data is not yet available. It is either currently being processed...'), '400:Timeout' ('Time out. The request cannot be processed.') and '400:CancelledRequest' ('Request aborted') are provider_transient, i.e. RETRYABLE -- core reads 400 as invalid_request, which is not retried at all, so a pull that hit a processing window simply died; '404:ResourceNotFound_*' and '409:ElementAlreadyExists_*' are invalid_request, where core leaves 404 and 409 'unclassified', i.e. retried until the dead letter for a resource that will never appear. AUTH_REVOKED IS STILL NOT DECLARED, and that is the same finding as 2026-08-01, re-verified against the full table: Piano's only authentication Category is BadAuthentication_* (401, 'Incorrect login or password'), and no published Category means a revoked or disabled key. Do not invent one -- add it the day a live pass (AI-13) shows it. 509 QuotasExceeded_TooManyRequests and 429 QuotasExceeded_TooManySimultaneousRequests stay on the core.quota.RateLimitError breaker path and are NEVER keyed here. ORIGINAL AI-114 NOTE (2026-08-01, kept for the record): piano is the case where the FORM was never the problem -- its ten keys were correctly shaped '<status>:<Category>' and correctly read by core. They were removed because not one of them could CHANGE a verdict: 401 BadAuthentication -> auth_expired, 403 UnauthorizedSite/InvalidSpace -> permission_denied, 400 Invalid* -> invalid_request and 500 UnknownError -> provider_transient are, every one of them, exactly what core.pull_errors._base_class_for_status already returns from the HTTP status alone. A map that restates pure HTTP proves nothing its absence would not; declaring it made the taxonomy look refined where it was not. The class that would prove a real refinement is auth_revoked -- the only one pure HTTP never produces -- and no documented Piano API-Code Category means a revoked key. Add entries here the day a live pass (AI-13) shows a Category whose class differs from its status, NOT before: a decorative map is worse than an empty one. THE MACHINERY STAYS AND IS STILL USED: connector._extract_api_code / _code_prefix still run, because the 400 InvalidColumns family is THE dynamic-catalog drift signal (pull_invalid_request_drift log + InvalidRequestError), and because they are what makes a future key matchable on the day one exists. Story 28.1 (dossier section 7): keys are '<http_status>:<API_Code_Category>' -- the CATEGORY PREFIX only. Piano v3 error bodies carry an API-Code string (Category_Subcode); connector._code_prefix() reduces it to its Category before matching, so every key here is a bare Category (BadAuthentication, UnauthorizedSite, InvalidSpace, InvalidColumns, ...) -- NEVER a full Category_Subcode (a full-code key would be unreachable). 401 BadAuthentication_* -> auth_expired (rotate/re-enter key). 403 UnauthorizedSite / InvalidSpace_* -> permission_denied (the site access-check signal). 400 InvalidColumns_* is THE dynamic-catalog drift key: an unknown Data Model property/metric key -> invalid_request + pull_invalid_request drift (NOT a crash, NOT a silent drop). 509 QuotasExceeded_TooManyRequests and any 429 stay on the core.quota.RateLimitError breaker path (NOT in this map): serialize per connection + backoff. 5xx fall through to pure-HTTP provider_transient. Only the Categories that CHANGE a verdict are declared: a key restating the class core already derives from the status alone cannot refine anything, and test_error_map_declares_only_matchable_prefix_keys refuses it. Dropped on 2026-08-17 for that reason: 400:InvalidColumns, 400:InvalidSpace, 400:UnknownColumns, 400:UnknownMetrics, 400:UnknownProperties, 401:BadAuthentication, 403:NoDataAccessBecauseUnpayment, 403:UnauthorizedSite, 500:UnknownError.

refetch._note: Dossier section 6: Piano is near-real-time event-collection analytics that stabilises within ~24h; there is no long conversion-restatement window (contrast google-ads). nightly 3d covers late/queued hits + offline-app sync + short reprocessing; weekly 14d / monthly 30d cover consent/identity reprocessing tails. Per-datastream overridable.

quota._note: Dossier section 4: Piano publishes NO QPS/points budget -- throttling is on CONCURRENT calls (QuotasExceeded_TooManyRequests HTTP 509). The 60/min budget is a conservative default; the real guard is per-connection serialization (no parallel fan-out) + the 509/429 breaker with backoff.

account_topology._comment: Story 28.1 (pattern 25.5): Piano reporting topology is organization -> site. The selected reporting entity is the SITE (space.s=[<site_id>]). There is NO documented public endpoint that enumerates the sites an API key can reach: v1 discovery verifies candidate site ids via a 1-day getData access-check probe (unreachable candidates dropped). PIANO_*_SITE_ID account fallbacks are FORBIDDEN in the pull path (doctrine); selection/access-check/trial/backfill are the core topology flows.

_max_provider_backfill_days_note: No max_provider_backfill_days is declared because Piano's 25-month rolling retention is a DEFAULT that is contract-configurable -- its own documentation says to 'contact your Account Manager to discuss feasibility and pricing' to extend it (https://analytics-docs.piano.io/en/analytics/v1/are-periods-limited-on-the-reporting-api). A per-customer value is not a manifest constant. Declaring a guessed window would promise a history the provider never committed to, so this module answers 'unknown' rather than a number (test_backfill_bound_is_declared_or_its_absence_is).
